title: A four-second track search finds no excess power 2 to 10 seconds after GW170817
abstract: We test public Hanford and Livingston strain for four-second tracks 2 to 10 seconds after GW170817. The bank has 1179 choices with constant or falling frequency. A minimum-detector power score has rank p = 0.372 against 233 nearby controls with an early noise estimate and p = 0.577 with a late estimate. No tested signal passes the 99 percent control threshold. All tested intervals pass the selected burst-quality flags. A four-second signal that falls from 1000 to 800 Hz is recovered in 9 of 80 tests at hrss = 1e-22 strain sqrt(s) per detector and in 80 of 80 tests at 3e-22. These counts apply to one artificial waveform with equal detector strain. They are not astrophysical upper limits. We do not constrain the remnant type or find a new source. The package includes code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and retrieval steps. Raw data stay outside the package.

display.caption: Left: cumulative control scores for two noise estimates. Dashed lines show target scores, 1.571 and 1.581. Right: recovery fractions for a four-second falling-frequency signal with equal strain in both detectors. Bars show approximate 95 percent Wilson intervals from 80 control intervals. These are limited signal tests, not astrophysical upper limits.
